cells.tense: You are at the desk now, deciding what to do with what the change left you holding.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Name something you gave lately and ask for its match — a hand, an hour back. Let someone say yes.
cells.core:
Something cost you to get, and you have kept it steady since. You're pointed at it now, not drifting, and the decision ahead isn't whether to keep it — it's what to do next with what you kept. You can say this, not that, without needing anyone's blessing. The give and take around you runs fairly even most days, and that evenness isn't a mood. It's a structure you keep standing by watching both sides.

This week, let an exchange close its loop. Name something you gave — time, a favor, a real answer — and ask for its match: a hand, an hour back. It isn't a test of anyone, just the other half of a sentence you already began. Let someone say yes. What you do with that yes stays yours to decide.
cells.sheetLine: You've kept something worth deciding what to do with next.
cells.verb: keeping steady what a change left behind, until it can be spent or shared
cells.place: where you pick a direction and mean it — this, not that

cells.tense: You are gripping what the change gave you before it can be spent or shared.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Go toward the feeling the change left loose, once. Get close to it before you decide anything about it.
cells.core:
The steady keeping has gone tight. Direction is set, but the grip is closing on what might still be moving, and you're rehearsing the next version of events in a way that keeps the present one unspent. The readiness is real. So is the weight. But the point of what you kept was that it could eventually be used, not only fenced off from use.

Something in what the change left hasn't pulled you yet. One feeling, loose. Go toward it once — a conversation, a look, a sitting with it — before you decide anything about it. Not to fix it; to stand next to it. The grip can loosen after that.

cells.tense: You chose a direction once, and you are still standing where you chose it.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Hold the same sentence when someone leans against a decision you still mean. No extra reasons.
cells.core:
You know what you meant to keep, and the pen is down beside it. That decision was made before this season, and it hasn't walked forward with you. What you kept is still the right shape, but the force behind it went quiet, and the people near it feel the quiet more than the shape.

You don't need a new decision. You need the old one said once more. Take something you decided and still mean, and when someone leans against it, hold the same sentence — no extra reasons, no reopening. Let what you chose catch up with where you're standing.

cells.tense: You are steering already, and the steering carries no name on it.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: At the next small fork, take one side and follow it to the end. One sentence, no case to argue.
cells.core:
The direction is being set — by you — and you have been treating it as the room's own arrangement. You aren't lost. You're deciding, and the deciding has been happening without your name near it. The structure works, which is why nobody points at it, and lately you've counted yourself among the nobody.

Let one call carry your name. When the next small fork appears — two things that could both be true — take one side and follow it to the end. One sentence, no case to argue. The structure keeps working either way. The difference is that you'll be standing inside what you chose.
